oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The closest visible structural context is tasimelteon (BMS-214778), which shares the propanamide and dihydrobenzofuran-containing melatonin receptor agonist scaffold with the query; its mean absolute oral bioavailability in humans is approximately 38% (90% CI 27–54%), above the 20% threshold.

Tasimelteon/BMS-214778 absolute oral bioavailability was 58.5% in rats at 1 mg/kg, while the monkey value was 11.7%; the human value is the most transferable reference for the query and remains above threshold.

In the fasted state, linezolid shows near-complete absolute oral bioavailability (93–103%) in healthy subjects, supporting that fasted oral absorption can be high for small amide-containing drugs, although linezolid is structurally distant.

No visible record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence that the query itself has F<20%; low-F records (e.g., HCPT, nebivolol, equol in rats) are structurally or species distant and do not override the closest analog's human F.
